cheatSheet.oneLineDefinition: Anomaly detection in data quality is the automated identification of statistically unexpected deviations in pipeline metrics (row counts, null rates, distributions, freshness) using learned baselines and seasonality-aware detectors to catch data quality incidents before they reach consumers.
keyConcepts: Z-score: (x - mean) / std; flag if |z| > 3 (3-sigma rule).
MAD: median +/- k * 1.4826 * median(|x - median(x)|); robust to outliers in history.
IQR bounds: Q1 - 1.5*IQR, Q3 + 1.5*IQR (Tukey fences); assumption-free.
PSI: sum( (A_i - E_i) * ln(A_i/E_i) ); < 0.1 stable, 0.1-0.2 moderate, > 0.2 significant shift.
KS test: maximum CDF difference between two empirical distributions; p-value < 0.05 flags shift.
Same-day-of-week (DOW) grouping: the simplest effective seasonality fix for daily metrics.
Cold-start: need ~14-28 days of same-DOW history before dynamic detectors are reliable; use static fallback during warm-up.
EWMA: alpha * x_t + (1-alpha) * EWMA_{t-1}; catches gradual drift by comparing to slow-moving baseline.
formulas: Z-score: z = (x - mean) / std; anomaly if |z| > k (k=3 typical)
IQR lower bound: Q1 - 1.5 * (Q3 - Q1); upper bound: Q3 + 1.5 * (Q3 - Q1)
MAD: median_absolute_deviation = median(|x_i - median(x)|); robust_z = (x - median) / (1.4826 * MAD)
PSI = sum( (actual_pct_i - expected_pct_i) * ln(actual_pct_i / expected_pct_i) ) over bins
EWMA: S_t = alpha * x_t + (1 - alpha) * S_{t-1}; alpha in (0, 1), higher = more reactive

# Python: PSI computation
def psi(baseline, current, n_bins=10, eps=1e-6):
    bins = np.linspace(min(baseline.min(), current.min()),
                       max(baseline.max(), current.max()), n_bins+1)
    bp = np.histogram(baseline, bins)[0] / len(baseline) + eps
    cp = np.histogram(current, bins)[0] / len(current) + eps
    return float(((cp - bp) * np.log(cp / bp)).sum())
interviewPoints: Static thresholds catch known-unknowns; dynamic detectors catch unknown-unknowns.
Always apply same-DOW grouping for daily metrics before building rolling baselines.
MAD > z-score when history contains outliers that would inflate std.
PSI > 0.2 = significant distribution shift; KS test for hypothesis-based shift testing.
Cold-start requires a static fallback for the first 14-28 days; never silently skip detection.
Alert fatigue is the biggest operational failure mode; tune k-sigma per metric via backtesting.
quickNotes: Monitor row count + null rates first; add distribution shift for ML features and KPI columns.
Same-day-of-week baseline is 80% of the solution for weekly seasonal false positives.
PSI bin edges must be fixed from the baseline period and reused for all future comparisons.
Precompute DOW statistics daily to make detection queries fast (join, not window recompute).
Track false positive rate weekly and tune k-sigma or add seasonality handling for noisy metrics.
Anomaly detection on metrics is detective—it fires after data lands; combine with inline dbt/GE tests for preventive blocking.

keyTakeaways: Anomaly detection on data quality metrics catches unknown-unknowns—incidents no static rule would have anticipated—by learning the normal behavior of pipeline metrics over time and flagging statistically significant deviations in row counts, null rates, distinct counts, freshness lag, and value distributions.

Seasonality-aware baselines (same-day-of-week rolling windows) are the single most impactful improvement over naive z-score detectors: without DOW grouping, predictable weekend volume dips generate constant false positives that cause alert fatigue and erode trust in the monitoring system.

Distribution shift detection (PSI, KS test) is essential beyond volume monitoring: a distribution shift in transaction amounts, user ages, or ML feature values can silently corrupt analytics and degrade model performance even when row counts and null rates look normal.

Cold-start is a production failure mode, not a minor edge case: new tables must have static threshold fallbacks during the first 14-28 days before same-DOW history is sufficient for dynamic detectors to produce reliable bounds.

Anomaly detection complements, but does not replace, explicit pipeline tests (dbt, Great Expectations, Soda): inline tests are preventive and block known bad data; anomaly detection is detective and catches novel failures after data lands—a mature data quality strategy combines both layers.
